sentences.zh: 序言 自周室建同姓，穆屬維城；

translations.literal: Preface: From the time the Zhou house established its clansmen of the same surname, distant kin were made bulwarks of the realm;
translations.idiomatic: Preface: Ever since the Zhou established its kinsmen of the same surname, distant branches were appointed as bulwarks of the state;

sentences.zh: 炎漢以降，帝王之子，靡不錫以王爵。

translations.literal: From the glorious Han onward, the sons of emperors and kings were without exception granted princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: From the Han dynasty onward, the sons of sovereigns were invariably enfeoffed with princely titles.

sentences.zh: 考帝繫者，於以見親親之誼焉。

translations.literal: Those who examine imperial genealogies may thereby perceive the principle of cherishing one's kin.
translations.idiomatic: In tracing imperial lineages, one may discern the principle of honoring kinship.

sentences.zh: 清初封爵之制，未嘗釐定，武功、慧哲、宣獻諸王，皆以功績而獲崇封。

translations.literal: In the early Qing, the system of enfeoffment had not yet been fixed; the Princes of Military Merit, Sagacious Wisdom, and Illustrious Merit all received exalted titles for their achievements.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Qing, enfeoffment had not yet been standardized; the Princes of Military Merit, Sagacious Wisdom, and Illustrious Merit all received high titles for their service.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，定九等爵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde, nine ranks of nobility were established.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongde, a nine-rank system of nobility was instituted.

sentences.zh: 順治六年，復定為親、郡王至奉恩將軍凡十二等，有功封，有恩封，有考封。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Shunzhi, it was again fixed at twelve ranks from prince of the first rank and prince of the second rank down to gentry officer of the imperial clan, with enfeoffment for merit, enfeoffment by grace, and enfeoffment by examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Shunzhi, the system was redefined as twelve ranks from princes of the first and second rank down to gentry officers of the imperial clan, comprising enfeoffment for merit, enfeoffment by grace, and enfeoffment by examination.

sentences.zh: 惟睿、禮、鄭、豫、肅、莊、克勤、順承八王，以佐命殊勳，世襲罔替。

translations.literal: Only the eight princes Rui, Li, Zheng, Yu, Su, Zhuang, Keqin, and Shuncheng, for their extraordinary service in aiding the founding of the dynasty, received perpetual hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: Only the eight princely houses of Rui, Li, Zheng, Yu, Su, Zhuang, Keqin, and Shuncheng, for their outstanding service in establishing the dynasty, enjoyed perpetual hereditary succession.

sentences.zh: 其他親、郡王，則世降一等，有至鎮國公、輔國公而仍延世賞者。

translations.literal: Other princes of the first and second rank descended one rank each generation; some reached defender of the state or bulwark of the state and still received hereditary rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Other princes of the first and second rank descended one rank per generation; some fell as far as defender or bulwark of the state yet still retained hereditary honors.

sentences.zh: 若以旁支分封，則降至奉恩將軍，迨世次已盡，不復承襲。

translations.literal: If enfeoffed from a collateral branch, the rank descended to gentry officer of the imperial clan; when the allotted generations were exhausted, succession ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When enfeoffment came from a collateral line, the rank descended to gentry officer of the imperial clan, and once the allotted generations were exhausted, succession ended.

sentences.zh: 蓋自景祖以上子孫謂之「覺羅」，與顯祖以下子孫謂之「宗室」者，親疏攸別，爵秩亦殊，數傳而後，僅得子、男。

translations.literal: Descendants from Jingzu upward were called "Gioro," while those from Xianzu downward were called "imperial clansmen"; near and distant kin were thus distinguished, ranks differed, and after several generations one might attain only viscount or baron.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants from Jingzu and above were called "Gioro," while those from Xianzu downward were called "imperial clansmen"; kinship was graded accordingly, ranks differed, and after several generations one might hold no more than a viscountage or barony.

sentences.zh: 原夫錫爵之本意，酬庸為上，展親次之，故有皇子而僅封貝勒、貝子、公者。

translations.literal: The original intent of granting titles was to reward merit first and extend kinship second; hence some imperial sons received only beile, beizi, or duke.
translations.idiomatic: The original purpose of enfeoffment was to reward merit first and extend kinship second; hence some sons of the emperor received no more than beile, beizi, or duke.

sentences.zh: 揆諸前禩，至謹極嚴。

translations.literal: Measured against previous dynasties, the practice was exceedingly cautious and strict.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with earlier dynasties, the practice was exceedingly cautious and strict.

sentences.zh: 雍正後，惟怡賢親王以公忠體國，恭忠親王以贊襄大政，醇賢親王以德宗本生考，皆世襲罔替。

translations.literal: After the Yongzheng reign, only Prince Yixian for serving the state with public loyalty, Prince Gongzhong for assisting in great affairs of state, and Prince Chunxian as the biological father of Emperor Dezong all received perpetual hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongzheng, only Prince Yixian for his loyal service to the state, Prince Gongzhong for assisting in major affairs of government, and Prince Chunxian as the biological father of Emperor Guangxu received perpetual hereditary succession.

sentences.zh: 至末年，而慶親王奕劻乃亦膺茲懋賞矣。

translations.literal: By the dynasty's final years, Prince Qing Yikuang also received this splendid reward.
translations.idiomatic: By the dynasty's closing years, Prince Qing Yikuang had also received this exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 自餘宗潢繁衍，非國有大慶，不得恩封；

translations.literal: As for the rest of the proliferating imperial clansmen, without a great national celebration they could not receive enfeoffment by grace;
translations.idiomatic: Among the rest of the ever-expanding imperial clan, enfeoffment by grace was granted only on occasions of great national celebration;

sentences.zh: 非嫻習騎射，不得考封。

translations.literal: without proficiency in horsemanship and archery they could not receive enfeoffment by examination.
translations.idiomatic: and without proficiency in horsemanship and archery, they could not receive enfeoffment by examination.

sentences.zh: 而入關二百餘年，習尚文勝，無復開國勇健之風，每屆歲終，與於選者益□ 。

translations.literal: Yet more than two hundred years after entering the pass, customs favored literary pursuits over martial ones, and the bold vigor of the founding era was gone; at each year's end, those who qualified in the examinations grew ever fewer.
translations.idiomatic: Yet more than two centuries after crossing the pass, literary pursuits had eclipsed martial ones, the bold spirit of the founding era was gone, and with each year's end examination fewer and fewer qualified for enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 此盛衰強弱之原歟？

translations.literal: Is this not the root of rise and decline, strength and weakness?
translations.idiomatic: Was this not the source of the dynasty's rise and decline, its strength and weakness?

sentences.zh: 今自肇祖以下子孫，列為世表，本諸瑤牒，支別派分。

translations.literal: Now the descendants from Zhaozu downward are arranged in a genealogical table, based on the imperial registers, with branches and lines distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: The descendants from Zhaozu downward are now arranged in a genealogical table, drawn from the imperial registers and sorted by branch and line.

sentences.zh: 其不列於十二等之封者，謂之「閒散宗室」，則從略焉。

translations.literal: Those not listed among the twelve ranks of enfeoffment are called "unattached imperial clansmen" and are passed over briefly.
translations.idiomatic: Those not holding one of the twelve ranks of enfeoffment are called "unattached imperial clansmen" and are treated only briefly here.

sentences.zh: 作皇子世表。

translations.literal: Thus is composed the Genealogical Table of Imperial Princes.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Genealogical Table of Imperial Princes.

translations.literal: Zhake'na. Second son of Zhasaketu. In the fourth year of Chongde, enfeoffed as Duke Who Guards the State. Soon demoted to Duke Who Supports the State on account of misconduct. In the seventh year, expelled from the imperial clan on account of a crime. In the second year of Shunzhi, readmitted to the imperial clan and enfeoffed as Duke Who Supports the State. In the sixth year, promoted to beizi. In the ninth year, stripped of rank on account of a crime; in the fourteenth year, granted Duke Who Supports the State rank on account of military merit. In the sixteenth year, died on campaign.

translations.literal: Saisangwu. Fifth son of Surhuaci. In the tenth year of Tianming, died. Posthumously enfeoffed as Beile of the First Rank; posthumous title He Hui.

translations.literal: Luotuo. Son of Saisangwu. In the first year of Chongde, enfeoffed as beizi. In the seventh year, stripped of rank on account of misconduct. In the eighth year of Shunzhi, enfeoffed as third-class Defender General. In the sixteenth year, promoted to first class. In the fourth year of Kangxi, died.

translations.literal: Fudali. Seventh son of Luotuo. In the fourth year of Kangxi, inherited General Who Assists the State. In the eighth year, promoted to Assistant General. In the twenty-fifth year, stripped of rank on account of misconduct.

cells.content: 濟爾哈朗。舒爾哈齊第六子。初封貝勒。崇德元年，以軍功晉鄭親王。順治元年，加封信義輔政叔王。五年，緣事降郡王。旋復親王爵。九年，加封叔鄭親王。十二年，薨。諡曰獻。乾隆四十三年，以佐命殊功，配享太廟。

translations.literal: Jirhalang. Sixth son of Surhuaci. Initially enfeoffed as beile. In the first year of Chongde, for military merit promoted to Prince Zheng. In the first year of Shunzhi, given the additional title Uncle Prince Regent of Faith and Righteousness. In the fifth year, demoted to prince of the second rank on account of misconduct. Soon restored to princely rank. In the ninth year, given the additional title Uncle Prince Zheng. In the twelfth year, died. Posthumous title Xian. In the forty-third year of Qianlong, for extraordinary service in aiding the founding, given joint enshrinement in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

In the fifth year he was demoted to prince of the second rank on account of misconduct but was soon restored to princely rank. In the ninth year he was given the additional title Uncle Prince Zheng. He died in the twelfth year and was given the posthumous title Xian. In the forty-third year of Qianlong he was granted joint enshrinement in the Imperial Ancestral Temple for extraordinary service in aiding the founding.

translations.literal: Labu. Second son of Jidu. In the seventh year of Kangxi, enfeoffed as third-class Assistant General. In the ninth year, inherited Prince Jian. In the twentieth year, died. In the twenty-second year, stripped of princely rank posthumously on account of misconduct.

cells.content: 巴爾堪。濟爾哈朗第四子。順治十二年，封三等輔國將軍。康熙七年，緣事降二等奉國將軍。八年，復封三等輔國將軍。十六年，緣事革退。十九年，卒。四十九年，追封三等輔國將軍。雍正元年，追封不入八分輔國公。諡曰武襄。巴爾堪墓碑陰刻有乾隆十七年追封簡親王之號。

translations.literal: Ba'erkan. Fourth son of Jirhalang. In the twelfth year of Shunzhi, enfeoffed as third-class Assistant General. In the seventh year of Kangxi, demoted to second-class General Who Assists the State on account of misconduct. In the eighth year, re-enfeoffed as third-class Assistant General. In the sixteenth year, stripped of rank on account of misconduct. In the nineteenth year, died. In the forty-ninth year, posthumously enfeoffed as third-class Assistant General. In the first year of Yongzheng, posthumously enfeoffed as Assistant General outside the eight privileges. Posthumous title Wuxiang. On the reverse of Ba'erkan's tomb stele is inscribed the title Prince Jian, posthumously granted in the seventeenth year of Qianlong.

In the seventeenth year of Qianlong, posthumously enfeoffed as Prince Jian.

In the third year, because Chengzhi inherited Prince Zheng, changed to inherit Chengzhi's Assistant General rank outside the eight privileges. In the fifth year, died.

In the fifteenth year of Qianlong, because his great-grandson Depè inherited Prince Jian, again posthumously enfeoffed as Prince Jian.

cells.content: 穆精阿。誠興子。乾隆四十六年，襲奉恩將軍。五十一年，卒。

translations.literal: Mujing'a. Son of Chengxing. In the forty-sixth year of Qianlong, inherited Garrison General. In the fifty-first year, died.

cells.content: 阿克色布庫。穆精阿第一子。乾隆五十二年，襲奉恩將軍。嘉慶二十四年，卒。

translations.literal: Akesebuku. First son of Mujing'a. In the fifty-second year of Qianlong, inherited Garrison General. In the twenty-fourth year of Jiaqing, died.

cells.content: 文霖。阿克色布庫嗣子。道光十五年，襲奉恩將軍。同治八年，卒。襲次巳盡，不襲。

translations.literal: Wenlin. Adopted heir of Akesebuku. In the fifteenth year of Daoguang, inherited Garrison General. In the eighth year of Tongzhi, died. Succession turns exhausted; no inheritance.
translations.idiomatic: Wenlin, adopted heir of Akesebuku. In the fifteenth year of Daoguang he inherited the Garrison General rank and died in the eighth year of Tongzhi; the succession turns were exhausted and no one inherited.

cells.content: 德沛。福存第八子。雍正十三年，封鎮國將軍。乾隆十二年，襲神保住之簡親王爵。十七年，薨。諡曰儀。無嗣。

translations.literal: Depè. Eighth son of Fucun. In the thirteenth year of Yongzheng, enfeoffed as Defender General. In the twelfth year of Qianlong, inherited Shenbaozhu's Prince Jian title. In the seventeenth year, died. Posthumous title Yi. No heir.

cells.content: 德全。福存第九子。康熙四十七年，封奉恩將軍。五十二年，卒。無嗣。

translations.literal: Dequan. Ninth son of Fucun. In the forty-seventh year of Kangxi, enfeoffed as Garrison General. In the fifty-second year, died. No heir.

cells.content: 德延。福存第十子。康熙四十九年，封奉恩將軍。五十三年，卒。無嗣。

translations.literal: Deyan. Tenth son of Fucun. In the forty-ninth year of Kangxi, enfeoffed as Garrison General. In the fifty-third year, died. No heir.

cells.content: 努賽。費揚武第六子。初封輔國公。順治六年，晉貝子。七年，卒。諡曰悼哀。

translations.literal: Nusai. Sixth son of Feiyangwu. Initially enfeoffed as Duke Who Supports the State. In the sixth year of Shunzhi, promoted to beizi. In the seventh year, died. Posthumous title Dao Ai.

cells.content: 拉篤祜。努賽第一子。順治八年，襲鎮國公。十七年，卒。諡曰端純。無嗣。

translations.literal: Laduhu. First son of Nusai. In the eighth year of Shunzhi, inherited Duke Who Guards the State. In the seventeenth year, died. Posthumous title Duan Chun. No heir.
translations.idiomatic: Laduhu, first son of Nusai. In the eighth year of Shunzhi he inherited the Duke Who Guards the State title, died in the seventeenth year, was given the posthumous title Duan Chun, and left no heir.

cells.content: 雅爾哈齊。顯祖第四子。無嗣。順治十年，追封通達郡王。十一年，以開創功配享太廟。

translations.literal: Ya'erhaqi. Fourth son of Xianzu. No heir. In the tenth year of Shunzhi, posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Universal Penetration. In the eleventh year, given joint enshrinement in the Imperial Ancestral Temple for founding merit.
translations.idiomatic: Ya'erhaqi, fourth son of Xianzu, left no heir. In the tenth year of Shunzhi he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Universal Penetration, and in the eleventh year was granted joint enshrinement in the Imperial Ancestral Temple for founding merit.

cells.content: 巴雅喇。顯祖第五子。以軍功賜號篤義。天命八年，卒。順治十年，追封貝勒。諡曰剛果。

translations.literal: Bayala. Fifth son of Xianzu. For military merit granted the title Du Yi. In the eighth year of Tianming, died. In the tenth year of Shunzhi, posthumously enfeoffed as beile. Posthumous title Gang Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Bayala, fifth son of Xianzu. He was granted the title Du Yi for military merit, died in the eighth year of Tianming, was posthumously enfeoffed as beile in the tenth year of Shunzhi, and was given the posthumous title Gang Guo.

cells.content: 拜音圖。巴雅喇第二子。順治二年，封一等鎮國將軍。四年，晉鎮國公。五年，晉貝子。六年，晉貝勒。九年，以罪削爵，黜宗室。嘉慶四年，復入宗室。

translations.literal: Baiyintu. Second son of Bayala. In the second year of Shunzhi, enfeoffed as first-class Defender General. In the fourth year, promoted to Duke Who Guards the State. In the fifth year, promoted to beizi. In the sixth year, promoted to beile. In the ninth year, stripped of noble rank on account of a crime and expelled from the imperial clan. In the fourth year of Jiaqing, readmitted to the imperial clan.
